question: A scientist performed an experiment to produce hybrid viruses by mixing two different serotypes of influenza virus, H1N1 and H2N2, in a respiratory epithelium cell line. Several days later, the scientist collected the media and analyzed the viral progeny. She found the following serotypes of virus: H1N1, H2N2, H1N2, and H2N1. Which of the following terms best explains the appearance of new serotypes?
analysis: The appearance of new serotypes, such as H1N2 and H2N1, from the mixing of two different serotypes of influenza virus (H1N1 and H2N2) is best explained by reassortment. Reassortment occurs when two different strains of segmented viruses, like influenza, infect the same cell and exchange genetic segments, leading to the creation of new viral combinations. This is a common mechanism for generating diversity in influenza viruses.
